target.title: fix(signal): forward reply metadata for durable sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now preserve quote metadata across the durable and outbound send paths, not only the narrow direct send path. Durable replies carry both `replyToId` and the Signal quote author where available, so direct chats can derive the author from the target and group replies can use the inbound sender metadata needed for native quotes.

This also makes queued/recovered sends and retargeted payloads behave consistently: recovery replays the same reply author context, implicit single-use replies consume both id and author together, and explicit payload retargets do not inherit a stale ambient author.

## What Changed

- Signal send surfaces: message adapter text/media, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media all forward native reply metadata into Signal send options.
- Durable delivery context: core channel send contexts, outbound contexts, reply policy, and delivery queue entries now carry optional `replyToAuthor` alongside `replyToId`.
- Reply routing rules: implicit single-use replies clear both `replyToId` and `replyToAuthor` after the first delivered unit, while explicit retargeted payloads clear ambient author metadata unless the reply id still matches the current inbound message.
- Recovery and reconciliation: queued delivery persistence, recovery replay, and unknown-send reconciliation preserve `replyToAuthor` so a restart does not downgrade Signal group replies into ordinary messages.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal durable sends with `replyToId` now reach the Signal sender with native quote metadata.
- Formatted Signal text/media and attached result text/media sends now forward native quote metadata as well, covering the previously missed sink paths.
- Durable inbound Signal group replies derive `replyToAuthor` from the current inbound sender only when the resolved `replyToId` still targets that current inbound message.
- Delivery queue recovery persists and replays `replyToAuthor`, including unknown-send reconciliation.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification
